subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers replace the conflicting open fork PR with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or adopt/rebase that fork PR as the landing candidate for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but GitHub still has an open non-maintainer fork PR with closing syntax, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author or a maintainer to rebase it to current main, cover the current async path, and add real TUI/Gateway proof before review.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR despite its conflict state, stale head, and lack of maintainer edit access.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: He committed the original picker/title work and authored adjacent transcript-field caching, making him the strongest available owner for the branch-path choice.
